subject: Decision framework: selecting link mode for Silverspring private deployment
messages:
From: markus_klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>, ben_carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Alex Dev <alex.dev@silverspring.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Decision framework: selecting link mode for Silverspring private deployment

Team —

Silverspring sent their requirements last week (attached). They want a private deployment inside their AWS account (VPCs in us-east-1 + us-west-2) with strong controls for egress, audit logs, and predictable latency for inference calls. They asked us for a recommendation between three primary link choices: VPC Peering, Interface VPC Endpoint (PrivateLink), and site-to-site VPN (IPSec/MPLS).

I put a first-pass matrix in the attached spreadsheet; highlights for our discussion:
- Peering: low-latency and native VPC routing, but not transitive and can complicate cross-account multi-region.
- PrivateLink: strong isolation (no route propagation into tenant VPC), simpler security boundaries, supports NLB->ENI patterns, but adds per-GB charges and requires endpoints per region.
- S2S VPN: easiest to stand up for on-prem-like setups, supports BGP for failover, but has variable latency, throughput caps (depends on gateway), and heavier ops burden for HA.

Ask: can you both review the matrix and reply with the top operational risks you see for each option, plus an explicit recommendation for our standard cadence (fast pilot vs production). Alex — feel free to add any constraints I missed (esp. procurement or compliance bullets).

I'll collate and propose a single recommended path tomorrow so we can move to an architecture sketch and SOW.

Thanks,
Markus

--
Markus Klein
Principal Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference
From: kimberly_park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
To: markus_klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>, ben_carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Alex Dev <alex.dev@silverspring.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 12:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Decision framework: selecting link mode for Silverspring private deployment

Thanks Markus — quick read of the sheet below. Operational risk notes: 

VPC Peering:
- Routing: peering is fine inside a single region/account pair, but cross-account transitive routing is not supported. If Silverspring expects traffic to hop through multiple VPCs we must either create many pairings or use a hub VPC (adds management).
- Security controls: flows are inside AWS network (no NAT) so auditing requires VPC flow logs + ENI-level monitoring. If they require strict egress controls to a dedicated egress/bastion, peering needs careful route table hygiene.
- Troubleshooting: packet path is straightforward which helps latency troubleshooting.

PrivateLink (Interface Endpoint):
- Isolation: excellent — we expose a service endpoint and Silverspring never has our routes in their tables. Good fit if they want minimal lateral footprint.
- Scaling: we need an NLB per region and account, and endpoints incur per-ENI costs and hourly charges; add egress/processing costs on our side.
- TLS mutual auth / mTLS: can be layered but requires SNI or ALPN conventions; certificate provisioning path should be documented in the SOW.

Site-to-site VPN (IPSec/BGP):
- Throughput & latency: depends on customer VPN appliance and AWS VGW/Transit; for inference workloads sustained high throughput can be expensive and jittery.
- Failover: BGP over redundant tunnels is standard but ops needs runbooks for rekeying and testing.
- Security: acceptable if they manage appliances and rotate keys; however, it pushes more responsibility to customer ops.

My recommendation for Silverspring pilot: use PrivateLink for the pilot region (us-east-1) to keep isolation and make the pilot low-risk for their network team. For production, consider a hybrid pattern: PrivateLink for control-plane calls + peering or Transit Gateway for high-throughput data paths if they need bulk tokenized payloads with lower cost per-GB.

I'll add a short appendix on certs and endpoint quotas into the sheet.

Kim

Kimberly Park
Head of Dedicated Deployments
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Decision framework: selecting link mode for Silverspring private deployment

Adding infra ops perspective and cost anchors: 

- Egress billing: PrivateLink moves some of the per-GB cost onto endpoint/data-processing lines; peering keeps traffic internal to AWS and generally avoids interface endpoint charges but if traffic crosses AZs/regions costs still apply. Need to model expected requests/sec and avg payload size to estimate monthly delta.
- Transit Gateway: Not in the initial three options list but worth flagging. For multi-region, multi-account scale, TGW reduces peering sprawl and supports propagation + central inspection points. Downside is TGW hourly attachments + data processing cost.
- VPN hardware limits: ask Silverspring for appliance max concurrent tunnels and throughput per tunnel. If they have low-end devices, VPN is a non-starter for production inference.
- MTU and fragmentation: inference payloads (base64 attachments, embeddings) can expose MTU problems over IPsec — we should include a payload-size test in the pilot.

Operational suggestion: pilot with PrivateLink + small peering for non-latency-critical management traffic. If usage grows > X qps or sustained throughput > Y MB/s, propose moving data-plane to Transit Gateway-backed peering and keep PrivateLink for auth/control traffic. I'll stub cost numbers in the spreadsheet (estimates for 100k requests/day with 10KB avg payload).

Ben

Ben Carter

Subject: Re: Decision framework: selecting link mode for Silverspring private deployment

Thanks — good feedback. Summary / proposed next steps for the SOW and pilot: 

1) Pilot (4 weeks, us-east-1): PrivateLink-only for inference control plane + a small VPC Peering link to host health/ops probes and log export. Deliverables: topology sketch, cert provisioning doc, endpoint quota request ticket, payload-size MTU test. Attachments: connection-matrix.xlsx (detailed matrix), topology-sketch.png, silverspring_requirements.pdf.

2) Production gating criteria: move to TGW-backed data plane if any of the following occur:
   - sustained 95th percentile throughput > 50 MB/s for > 6 hours/day
   - request rate > 2k RPS sustained
   - ops requires centralized flow inspection across multiple accounts/regions

3) Security/compliance: we'll enable VPC Flow Logs -> S3 ingestion + CloudWatch metric filters, and provide a template KMS key policy for audit. We'll require Silverspring to share the endpoint-of-record for their firewall team and grant temporary test keys for the pilot.

Action items: Ben — finalize cost model and fill the X/Y numbers in the sheet. Kim — I'll pull together the certs and endpoint quota playbook and a draft SOW. Alex/N. Patel — if you can confirm their appliance model (if they choose VPN instead) and the expected qps/payload numbers that would help.

I'll schedule a 30 min sync on Friday to lock the SOW.

-Markus

--
Markus Klein
Principal Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference
